good.prompt:
Create a production CHARACTER ACTION ANIMATION SPRITE ATLAS, not a poster or lineup. The supplied reference is a style and character reference: preserve those five realistic 3D African adults and blue clothing. Genuine alpha transparency. EXACTLY 5 ROWS by 8 COLUMNS, a perfectly aligned regular grid of FORTY equally sized rectangular cells, no text, no labels, no grid lines or scenery. Each row is an eight-frame chronological loop of ONE action by the SAME character, with the SAME face/clothing/props/camera/scale/position across its eight frames. Full character including feet/props entirely contained within each cell with 10% transparent padding. Show ACTUAL articulated action changes in arms, legs, hands and props between consecutive frames, not shifting the whole image or repeating a static pose. Lock camera and ground baseline within each row. First and last pose should connect smoothly. Square high-resolution canvas preferred (roughly 2560x2560); the grid is 8 equal columns across and 5 equal rows down. Characters and furniture only on transparent background.
ROWS from top to bottom:
Row 1: woman jogging, full alternating leg stride and opposite arm swings. Eight distinct phases spanning the complete action.
Row 2: man playing football, stepping to ball, swinging right leg, contacting ball, ball rolls a little then returning to ready stance. Eight distinct phases spanning the complete action.
Row 3: woman performing yoga tree pose, arms rise from prayer to overhead and return, slight balance adjustments. Eight distinct phases spanning the complete action.
Row 4: woman cycling, knees and ankles visibly travel through a full pedaling revolution, wheels rotate, torso steady. Eight distinct phases spanning the complete action.
Row 5: man stretching, arms move from lowered to overhead, lean left then right, arms return. Eight distinct phases spanning the complete action.
Critical: reading rows must show a page actually being lifted, turned across the book spine and laid down. Walking/running/cycling must have real joint/limb pose changes, not bobbing still images. No extra rows or columns.
